selection_reason: p is 1 mod 3 and 7 mod 24; p=883 and p=907 are 1 mod 3 and 19 mod 24, while p=887 is 2 mod 3 and 23 mod 24
question: Does the uniform 24-point rational fiber pattern persist when p mod 3 stays 1 but p mod 8 changes from 3 to 7?
source_policy: All 919 j-values; one representative per generic quadratic-twist pair; three j=0 sextic representatives paired under quadratic twist; one j=1728 representative; cyclic nonbacktracking 16- and 27-isogeny chains
source_gate: Paired chain count must equal the independent weight-two Hecke point count minus the rational cusp count
image_policy: Evaluate every noncuspidal chain with both intermediate j-invariants, Frobenius conjugacy, the exact twist, and the dual 3-isogeny
image_gate: One filtered coordinate point per quarter-shift, one Frobenius pair, one rational B output per source, independent audit of source keys, B equation, fiber histogram, cusp image, and B group order
primary_outputs: full image and complement after cusp identity
interpretation_rule: A uniform 24-point histogram supports the p mod 3 hypothesis over the p mod 24=19 hypothesis for these tested primes; a nonuniform histogram rejects the former as a complete rule. Neither outcome alone proves a general congruence law.
